approachQuestion.prompt:
Room occupancy peak

Each booking is [arrival,departure), with arrival<departure. A room is free at the exact instant another booking arrives when the first departs. Return the maximum simultaneous bookings. 1≤n≤200000; times are integers in [0,10^9]. Examples: [[1,5],[5,8],[2,4]]→2; [[3,7]]→1.

Do not modify either input. Values are opaque comparison keys; hashing, radix, counting and bucket methods are outside the stated model. Choose the most efficient valid method that returns the required result for every allowed input.
constraints: Inputs are read-only and must remain unchanged.
Only comparison-based ordering is allowed; hashing, radix, counting and bucket methods are outside this problem model.

options.text: Sort all arrival and departure events chronologically, process departures before arrivals at equal times, and track the maximum active count.
options.feedback: Chronological order preserves the active interval set; for half-open bookings, departures at a shared time release rooms before new arrivals are counted.

options.text: Process arrivals before departures at equal times.
options.feedback: For [[1,5],[5,8]], this incorrectly counts two simultaneous bookings at time 5.

options.text: Sort bookings by arrival and compare each only with the immediately previous booking.
options.feedback: Comparing only consecutive arrivals misses an earlier long-running booking. For [[1,10],[2,8],[3,4]], the true peak is 3, but the last booking overlaps its immediate predecessor only, yielding 2.

options.text: For each booking, count all other bookings that overlap it and return the largest such count.
options.feedback: Intervals that overlap the same booking need not overlap one another. For [[1,10],[2,3],[4,5],[6,7]], the long booking overlaps three other bookings, so this reports 3, while the simultaneous maximum is 2.

feedback.reason: Departure-before-arrival at an equal timestamp permits reuse without overlap under the stated endpoint convention.
details: Sort endpoint events by time with departures before arrivals at ties; scan active count and retain its maximum.

Departure-before-arrival at an equal timestamp permits reuse without overlap under the stated endpoint convention. Reversing this tie order would invent simultaneous occupancy that the intervals do not have.

“Sort all arrival and departure events chronologically, process departures before arrivals at equal times, and track the maximum active count.”: Chronological order preserves the active interval set; for half-open bookings, departures at a shared time release rooms before new arrivals are counted.
“Process arrivals before departures at equal times.”: For [[1,5],[5,8]], this incorrectly counts two simultaneous bookings at time 5.

“Sort bookings by arrival and compare each only with the immediately previous booking.”: Comparing only consecutive arrivals misses an earlier long-running booking. For [[1,10],[2,8],[3,4]], the true peak is 3, but the last booking overlaps its immediate predecessor only, yielding 2.

“For each booking, count all other bookings that overlap it and return the largest such count.”: Intervals that overlap the same booking need not overlap one another. For [[1,10],[2,3],[4,5],[6,7]], the long booking overlaps three other bookings, so this reports 3, while the simultaneous maximum is 2.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed below, choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space bounds. Count working copies, event/heap/visited storage and sort buffers; exclude the caller input and returned output. Comparisons and arithmetic take constant time; merge sort uses a linear buffer.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Sort 2n endpoint events and maintain one active count.
details: n jobs create 2n endpoint records. Merge sorting them takes O(2n log(2n))=O(n log n), then the active-count scan is O(n). The records and sorting buffer are both auxiliary because output is a scalar. Processing end-before-start changes tie correctness but not this comparison count.
